To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the xrs mutants are more sensitive to the cell killing, chromosomnal aberration-inducing and SCE-inducing effects of bleomycin and mono- and bi-funtional alkylating agents than the parental CHO-K1 cells.
the xrs mutants are sensitive to the induction of chromosomal damage by X-rays and bleomycin, and to the induction of HPRT and Ouar mutants by MMS and X-rays.

xrs5 and xrs6 cells were sensitive to the cell killing effects of bleomycin, and to induction of chromosome aberrations by mono- and bifunctional alkylating agents, and to the induction of HPRT and Ou mutations by MMS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of the cellular response to DNA damage.
the elucidation of the mechanism by which the X-ray sensitivity of the mutants xrs 5/6 is expressed in terms of the induction of chromosome damage by chemical mutagens.
characterisation of CHO cell mutants with respect to their responses to various mutagens, including bleomycin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the xrs 5 mutant is a good model for the study of the cellular response to DNA damage induced by both radiations and chemicals.
the increased sensitivity of these mutants to the chemical agents used here is not related to the increased sensitivity to ionising radiation.
xrs 5 cells are more sensitive than xrs 6 to bleomycin and that xrs 6 are more sensitive than wild type CHO-K1 cells to the other chemicals tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutants xrs 5 (deficient in DNA-PKcs) and xrs 8 (deficient in Ku80) have the same response to bleomycin, while xrs 6 (deficient in both DNA-PKcs and Ku80) is more sensitive.

both mutants xrs 5, and xrs 61 are more sensitive for induction of chromosomnal aberrations, cell killing and mutations after treatment with mono- and bifunctional alkylating agents and bleomycin than wild-type CHO cells.

the xrs mutants are more sensitive than wild type CHO-K1 cells to the cytogenetical effect of all the agents tested and that the mutants are not only sensitive to mono-functional alkylating agent MMS but also to bi-functional alkylators such as EMS, MMC and to the DNA strand-breaking agent bleomycin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the xrs mutants show increased sensitivity to the cell killing and chromosomal aberrations induction effect of mono- and bifunctional alkylating agents, bleomycin and X-rays.
the mutants xrs 5, xrs 6 and CHO-K1 cells have a different response to bleomycin treatment in G1-phase cells.
the xrs mutants are more sensitive to mono- and bi- alkylating agents than to the DNA strand breaking agents.
